world.title: Ukraine’s President Zelenskyy says Russia targeted his plane twice
world.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CBS News that Russian drones entered Moldovan airspace twice in recent weeks while his presidential aircraft was in or near Chișinău. He said the first incident occurred as he traveled to Norway and the second as he returned to Ukraine, linking both to an effort to intimidat
world.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CBS News that Russian drones entered Moldovan airspace twice in recent weeks while his presidential aircraft was in or near Chișinău. He said the first incident occurred as he traveled to Norway and the second as he returned to Ukraine, linking both to an effort to intimidate him and other foreign leaders. Moldova temporarily closed its airspace on Sept. 9 after a drone alert delayed Zelenskyy’s departure for Oslo. Moldovan authorities said two drones entered the country that day: one landed in a field north of the capital and started a fire, while the other continued into Romanian airspace. Zelenskyy’s account of an incident during his return trip had not previously been reported, and there was no independent confirmation that his aircraft was directly targeted.

world.title: Trump administration prepares $2.8 billion bomb sale to Israel
world.summary: The Trump administration is preparing a proposed $2.8 billion weapons package for Israel that includes 40,000 2,000-pound bombs, according to U.S. officials and people familiar with the plan. The package includes 20,000 MK-84 general-purpose bombs, 20,000 BLU-117 bombs and 20,000 I-2000 penetrator warheads. Most of the
world.content: The Trump administration is preparing a proposed $2.8 billion weapons package for Israel that includes 40,000 2,000-pound bombs, according to U.S. officials and people familiar with the plan. The package includes 20,000 MK-84 general-purpose bombs, 20,000 BLU-117 bombs and 20,000 I-2000 penetrator warheads. Most of the purchase would be funded through Foreign Military Financing, which uses U.S. funds to help Israel buy American-made weapons. The administration has informally presented the deal to congressional committees, but officials said it was not yet final. The transfer would include weapons whose use in densely populated Gaza prompted the Biden administration to pause a shipment in 2024. President Trump lifted that restriction after returning to office in January 2025. Israel has used similar 2,000-pound bombs in Gaza and Lebanon during the regional conflict. The war in Gaza has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and continued despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire. The State Department said it does not confirm or comment on proposed arms sales before formal congressional notification.
world.image_alt: Trump administration prepares $2.8 billion bomb sale to Israel

world.title: Maduro ally Alex Saab pleads guilty in Miami case
world.summary: Alex Saab, a Colombian-Venezuelan businessman and former Venezuelan minister whom U.S. authorities identify as a close ally and alleged frontman for Nicolás Maduro, pleaded guilty on September 15 in federal court in Miami to conspiracy to launder money. The case involves alleged bribes and fraudulent contracts tied to
world.content: Alex Saab, a Colombian-Venezuelan businessman and former Venezuelan minister whom U.S. authorities identify as a close ally and alleged frontman for Nicolás Maduro, pleaded guilty on September 15 in federal court in Miami to conspiracy to launder money. The case involves alleged bribes and fraudulent contracts tied to Venezuela’s CLAP subsidized-food program during the country’s economic crisis. Under the agreement, Saab pleaded guilty to the single money-laundering count, agreed to cooperate with continuing U.S. investigations and to forfeit $195 million that prosecutors link to the scheme. The charge carries a maximum sentence of 20 years, but prosecutors agreed to recommend a sentence near the lower end of the applicable range and seek further reductions if his cooperation proves useful. The agreement does not publicly name Maduro, and Saab is scheduled to be sentenced in January 2027.
world.image_alt: Maduro ally Alex Saab pleads guilty in Miami case

world.title: House Democrats probe Russian funding of Trump Jr wedding
world.summary: House Democrats have opened an investigation into reports that Umar Kremlev, a Russian businessman who leads the International Boxing Association and whom the reports describe as close to President Vladimir Putin, paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for celebrations for Donald Trump Jr. and Bettina Anderson in the Ba
world.content: House Democrats have opened an investigation into reports that Umar Kremlev, a Russian businessman who leads the International Boxing Association and whom the reports describe as close to President Vladimir Putin, paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for celebrations for Donald Trump Jr. and Bettina Anderson in the Bahamas in May. The couple confirmed that Kremlev hosted two post-wedding nights. ProPublica reported that he covered expenses including a private-island rental and fireworks. Rep. Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, requested communications, financial records, a guest list and information about Trump Jr.'s security clearance from White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Trump Jr. Garcia said he was examining possible foreign entanglements, pay-to-play arrangements and national-security risks. Democrats cannot compel production of the requested material while they are in the House minority, though that could change after the November 3 midterm elections.
world.image_alt: House Democrats probe Russian funding of Trump Jr wedding

world.title: U.S. charges five over alleged Russian assassination network
world.summary: The U.S. Justice Department has charged five people prosecutors say worked for Russian intelligence services in a global network that planned targeted killings and terrorist attacks, including an alleged attempt to kill a Russian dissident believed to be in the Washington, D.C., area. A Manhattan federal indictment uns
world.content: The U.S. Justice Department has charged five people prosecutors say worked for Russian intelligence services in a global network that planned targeted killings and terrorist attacks, including an alleged attempt to kill a Russian dissident believed to be in the Washington, D.C., area. A Manhattan federal indictment unsealed Tuesday names former Russian intelligence colonel Yuri Khrameev, his son Kirill Khrameev, Cuban nationals Oemis Romagoza Durruthy and Yaidel Delgado Suarez, and Venezuelan national Angel Eduardo Castro. All five remain at large and are presumed innocent. Prosecutors allege the RIS Network has operated since at least 2024, paying or attempting to pay people in the United States and other countries to surveil Russian dissidents and arrange killings, and recruiting operatives for attacks on civilian and military infrastructure in European countries viewed as supporting Ukraine. In one case this summer, a U.S.-based recruit allegedly received $1,000 to $1,500 to photograph and record locations linked to the dissident, then was offered $40,000 to kill or make the person disappear. The recruit declined to carry out the killing.
world.image_alt: U.S. charges five over alleged Russian assassination network

world.title: Turkey detains LGBTQ protesters as crackdown expands nationwide
world.summary: Turkish police detained at least 150 people on Sept. 15 outside Istanbul’s Çağlayan courthouse after demonstrators gathered to demand the release of LGBTQ activists detained in weekend raids. Police surrounded the group, declared the protest unauthorized and intervened before protesters could deliver a statement. Two j
world.content: Turkish police detained at least 150 people on Sept. 15 outside Istanbul’s Çağlayan courthouse after demonstrators gathered to demand the release of LGBTQ activists detained in weekend raids. Police surrounded the group, declared the protest unauthorized and intervened before protesters could deliver a statement. Two journalists were among those detained. The protest followed operations in several provinces under the government’s “My Family Is Safe” campaign. Justice Minister Akin Gürlek said the campaign targeted 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses in 15 provinces, citing the protection of children, family values and public order. Authorities also raided LGBTQ association offices and venues and blocked websites and social-media accounts. On Sept. 14, a court in Izmir ordered 16 people held pending trial. Same-sex relations are legal in Turkey, while President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan has linked the campaign to his “Decade of the Family and Population” initiative.
world.image_alt: Turkey detains LGBTQ protesters as crackdown expands nationwide

world.title: U.S.-China AI rivalry blocks progress toward safety agreement
world.summary: The United States and China are rejecting calls to slow frontier artificial intelligence development, even as researchers and technology executives warn that increasingly capable systems may outpace existing safety controls. President Donald Trump has argued that regulation could surrender the lead to China, while Chin
world.content: The United States and China are rejecting calls to slow frontier artificial intelligence development, even as researchers and technology executives warn that increasingly capable systems may outpace existing safety controls. President Donald Trump has argued that regulation could surrender the lead to China, while Chinese state media has called the U.S. proposal a disguised effort to preserve American dominance ahead of an expected Trump-Xi meeting in Washington later this month. The disagreement reflects strategic competition and differing views of AI risk. U.S. officials and industry leaders focus on catastrophic loss of control, cyberattacks and other misuse, while Chinese authorities emphasize threats to state security, critical infrastructure, data and political stability. Beijing nevertheless says advanced AI should remain under human control and has promoted international guardrails. China has also narrowed the performance gap with U.S. models: A Stanford AI Index assessment cited by Thai PBS put the U.S. lead at about 2.7% in March, although the United States retained advantages in frontier-model volume, high-impact patents and data-center infrastructure.
world.image_alt: U.S.-China AI rivalry blocks progress toward safety agreement

world.title: U.S. confirms orbital weapons as Russia, China warn
world.summary: The United States has publicly acknowledged for the first time that it deployed “on-orbit space control weapons” capable of defending U.S. forces against hostile action. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink made the disclosure on Sept. 14 at the Air, Space & Cyber Conference in National Harbor, Maryland, but did not identify
world.content: The United States has publicly acknowledged for the first time that it deployed “on-orbit space control weapons” capable of defending U.S. forces against hostile action. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink made the disclosure on Sept. 14 at the Air, Space & Cyber Conference in National Harbor, Maryland, but did not identify the systems, explain how they operate, say how many exist or disclose when they reached orbit. The U.S. Space Force said the capabilities can be used for offensive and defensive purposes under the direction of combatant commands. For years, the United States has warned about Russian and Chinese counterspace programs. Two years ago, Washington said Russia was developing a new space-based anti-satellite weapon, though the White House said the danger was not imminent. Washington is also expanding autonomous military systems and planning space-based elements of the Golden Dome missile-defense system.
world.image_alt: U.S. confirms orbital weapons as Russia, China warn

business.title: UK state pension set to exceed £13,000 next April
business.summary: The UK state pension is set to rise by 3.9% next April after official earnings data showed average wages rose by that amount in the three months to July. Under the triple lock, the full new state pension would increase from £241.30 a week, or about £12,500 a year, to £250.70 a week, or roughly £13,000 a year. The old b
business.content: The UK state pension is set to rise by 3.9% next April after official earnings data showed average wages rose by that amount in the three months to July. Under the triple lock, the full new state pension would increase from £241.30 a week, or about £12,500 a year, to £250.70 a week, or roughly £13,000 a year. The old basic state pension would rise to £192.10 a week, or about £9,990 a year, for the roughly two-thirds of pensioners who reached qualifying age before April 2016. The government said pensioners who receive only the full new state pension would not pay income tax, despite the tax-free personal allowance being frozen at £12,570. The allowance was extended until 2031, raising concern that the pension increase could otherwise bring some retirees into the income-tax system. State pension spending totals £154 billion this year, while forecasts cited by the BBC indicate it could rise by a further £600 million a year by 2029-30.
business.image_alt: UK state pension set to exceed £13,000 next April

business.title: Update: EU rebuffs Canada’s proposed “unique alliance”
business.summary: European Union governments have pushed back against Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s proposal for a “unique alliance” that would deepen cooperation on trade, security and investment without full EU membership. Five EU diplomats told the Financial Times that governments were wary of granting Canada preferential mar
business.content: European Union governments have pushed back against Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s proposal for a “unique alliance” that would deepen cooperation on trade, security and investment without full EU membership. Five EU diplomats told the Financial Times that governments were wary of granting Canada preferential market access, although they supported closer cooperation with Canadian arms manufacturers and mining companies. Carney is visiting Strasbourg on September 16-17 as Canada seeks to reduce its dependence on the United States. Ottawa has said the proposed partnership could cover energy, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, defence and mobility for workers and students. Carney has ruled out EU membership and said any arrangement should be tailored to Canadian priorities. He is also urging the 10 EU countries that have not fully ratified the Canada-EU trade agreement to complete the process.
business.image_alt: Update: EU rebuffs Canada’s proposed “unique alliance”

business.title: AI leaders split over calls to slow development
business.summary: Former Google DeepMind researcher Bilal Chughtai said he believes advanced artificial intelligence could kill all humans and that time to prevent that outcome may be running out. Chughtai, who worked on artificial general intelligence safety and alignment and left Google DeepMind in July 2026, added to recent warnings
business.content: Former Google DeepMind researcher Bilal Chughtai said he believes advanced artificial intelligence could kill all humans and that time to prevent that outcome may be running out. Chughtai, who worked on artificial general intelligence safety and alignment and left Google DeepMind in July 2026, added to recent warnings from Anthropic researchers and former employee Jacob Coxon. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for slower development of advanced systems, with public support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk. The warnings focus on the possibility that AI systems could improve their successors, operate through autonomous agents and act beyond developers’ control. Critics said some extinction claims lack scientific evidence or rely on implausible assumptions: the UK AI Security Institute found Anthropic’s Mythos could autonomously compromise only small, weakly defended systems, while NYU professor Gary Marcus called claims that an AI swarm could take over the entire internet “nonsensical” without extreme negligence by laboratories. President Trump has rejected calls to slow development, arguing that the United States must maintain its lead over China. Opposition to new data centers has focused on electricity prices, water use and local infrastructure.
business.image_alt: AI leaders split over calls to slow development

business.title: Canada expands tax breaks as Carney courts global investors
business.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney used Canada’s first national investment summit in Toronto on Sept. 15 to pitch the country as a destination for global capital and reduce dependence on the United States. The government is targeting C$1 trillion in investment over the next five years, while summit participants represented mor
business.content: Prime Minister Mark Carney used Canada’s first national investment summit in Toronto on Sept. 15 to pitch the country as a destination for global capital and reduce dependence on the United States. The government is targeting C$1 trillion in investment over the next five years, while summit participants represented more than C$120 trillion in assets. Ottawa presented 167 projects spanning energy, critical minerals, ports, transportation, data centres and digital technology. Carney announced the Productivity Mega Deduction, expanding immediate or accelerated tax writeoffs to cover 65% of eligible asset classes, up from roughly 15%. Eligible assets include fibre-optic cables, mining property, pipelines, software and other infrastructure. Finance Canada estimates the changes will reduce the marginal effective tax rate on new business investment to 6.4% from about 13%; the government estimates the additional five-year fiscal cost at C$36 billion beginning in fiscal 2026-27. Carney also said Canada would seek private investment to operate its four largest airports while retaining public ownership of the land and assets.
business.image_alt: Canada expands tax breaks as Carney courts global investors

business.title: Nvidia and Meta reject calls for coordinated AI slowdown
business.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg rejected calls from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for an industry-wide slowdown in frontier AI development. Speaking at Salesforce’s Dreamforce conference in San Francisco on Sept. 15, Huang said companies should test products and delay release
business.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg rejected calls from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for an industry-wide slowdown in frontier AI development. Speaking at Salesforce’s Dreamforce conference in San Francisco on Sept. 15, Huang said companies should test products and delay releases when they are not confident about safety, but argued that market forces and company-level responsibility are sufficient without new laws. Zuckerberg said on X that competition, legal liability and the commercial value of trustworthy, aligned models give laboratories incentives to act independently rather than wait for a cross-industry pact. Amodei has proposed independent evaluators with employee-level access to AI companies, common safety standards among democratic countries and eventual international coordination; Altman and Elon Musk have backed elements of that approach. The dispute has also become a US-China technology-policy issue: President Trump rejected slowdown proposals as harmful to the US competitive position, while China’s Foreign Ministry described the US debate as fear-mongering. Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled to meet on Sept. 24.
business.image_alt: Nvidia and Meta reject calls for coordinated AI slowdown

business.title: OpenAI weighs funding round above $1.2 trillion valuation
business.summary: OpenAI is holding early discussions with investors about a new private funding round that could value the ChatGPT developer at about $1.2 trillion before an initial public offering. Investors initiated the talks, and the valuation and timing could change over the coming months; any decision to proceed depends on OpenAI
business.content: OpenAI is holding early discussions with investors about a new private funding round that could value the ChatGPT developer at about $1.2 trillion before an initial public offering. Investors initiated the talks, and the valuation and timing could change over the coming months; any decision to proceed depends on OpenAI's IPO timetable. The proposed valuation would exceed the $852 billion value assigned to OpenAI after its $122 billion financing in March. Chief Executive Sam Altman said on September 12 that OpenAI would not go public in 2026 and indicated that a listing before 2027 was unlikely, citing AI-safety concerns.
business.image_alt: OpenAI weighs funding round above $1.2 trillion valuation

business.title: Saudi Arabia reroutes oil after pipeline attack disrupts exports
business.summary: Saudi Arabia has suspended crude loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu and canceled some oil cargoes scheduled for European customers after drone attacks damaged its 1,200-kilometer East-West pipeline on Sept. 11. The pipeline links eastern oil fields with Yanbu and provided an alternative to shipping through the heavi
business.content: Saudi Arabia has suspended crude loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu and canceled some oil cargoes scheduled for European customers after drone attacks damaged its 1,200-kilometer East-West pipeline on Sept. 11. The pipeline links eastern oil fields with Yanbu and provided an alternative to shipping through the heavily disrupted Strait of Hormuz. Saudi officials have blamed the attack on Iraqi-based, Iran-aligned groups, while Saudi Aramco has not commented on the canceled cargoes. Riyadh is seeking to move more crude through Gulf terminals and the Strait of Hormuz and has offered Asian buyers ship-to-ship transfers near Oman, Bloomberg reported. Repair estimates range from several days to three to five weeks, with some assessments extending to six or eight weeks; U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the pipeline should resume soon. Oil prices rose above $100 a barrel before retreating on Sept. 16 after an unexpected 7.1-million-barrel increase in U.S. crude inventories.
business.image_alt: Saudi Arabia reroutes oil after pipeline attack disrupts exports

business.title: UK inflation rises to 3.1% as fuel prices surge
business.summary: UK consumer price inflation rose to 3.1% in August from 2.9% in July, the Office for National Statistics said, as motor-fuel prices increased sharply. The rate matched economists’ expectations and was the highest since March. Motor-fuel prices rose 23% from a year earlier as higher global energy costs, which reports li
business.content: UK consumer price inflation rose to 3.1% in August from 2.9% in July, the Office for National Statistics said, as motor-fuel prices increased sharply. The rate matched economists’ expectations and was the highest since March. Motor-fuel prices rose 23% from a year earlier as higher global energy costs, which reports linked to the Middle East conflict, fed through to household and business transport expenses.
business.image_alt: UK inflation rises to 3.1% as fuel prices surge

science.title: Scientists debate whether life’s origins can be known
science.summary: Scientists remain divided over how biology began and whether researchers could ever establish the answer with certainty, Scientific American reported. A related biology discussion examined why the probability of life arising on an Earth-like planet is unknown: Earth is the only observed example.
science.content: Scientists remain divided over how biology began and whether researchers could ever establish the answer with certainty, Scientific American reported. A related biology discussion examined why the probability of life arising on an Earth-like planet is unknown: Earth is the only observed example.

science.title: Study finds tropical extreme rainfall covers larger areas, lasts longer
science.summary: A study of observed hourly rainfall in Singapore from 1980 to 2024 found that tropical extreme storms cover larger areas and last longer as the climate warms, increasing the total volume of rain they produce while leaving peak intensity unchanged. In Sweden, agricultural researchers are testing a Retention-Irrigation S
science.content: A study of observed hourly rainfall in Singapore from 1980 to 2024 found that tropical extreme storms cover larger areas and last longer as the climate warms, increasing the total volume of rain they produce while leaving peak intensity unchanged. In Sweden, agricultural researchers are testing a Retention-Irrigation System designed to store and regulate water during dry periods and quickly release it during floods. The project will examine whether the system affects soil ecosystems and the movement of nitrous oxide, nitrate and phosphate into air and water.
science.image_alt: Study finds tropical extreme rainfall covers larger areas, lasts longer

science.title: New Tanzanian fossil species suggests younger age for rocks tied to dinosaur origins
science.summary: Paleontologists have described Dinodontosaurus isiyavamanda, a new plant-eating dicynodont species from Tanzania that lived about 240 million years ago during the Triassic period. The species was identified from a skull and partial skeleton collected in 1963 from the Lifua Member of Tanzania’s Manda Beds, and a second
science.content: Paleontologists have described Dinodontosaurus isiyavamanda, a new plant-eating dicynodont species from Tanzania that lived about 240 million years ago during the Triassic period. The species was identified from a skull and partial skeleton collected in 1963 from the Lifua Member of Tanzania’s Manda Beds, and a second specimen recovered in 2012. The animal belongs to Dinodontosaurus, a genus previously known only from South America. Its presence in eastern Africa links Tanzanian and South American fossil-bearing rocks and suggests that the Manda Beds may be younger than previously thought, potentially changing the age assigned to rocks associated with some of the earliest potential dinosaur fossils. Researchers led by the University of Bristol examined the fossils using CT scans, 3D surface imaging and phylogenetic analysis.
science.image_alt: New Tanzanian fossil species suggests younger age for rocks tied to dinosaur origins

science.title: Researchers propose searching Moon dust for alien technology
science.summary: A team led by Lewis Pinault, a SETI Institute affiliate scientist, has proposed searching lunar soil for microscopic remnants of technology from an ancient extraterrestrial civilization. The study, published as an arXiv preprint and under peer review, presents a quantitative framework for testing whether engineered par
science.content: A team led by Lewis Pinault, a SETI Institute affiliate scientist, has proposed searching lunar soil for microscopic remnants of technology from an ancient extraterrestrial civilization. The study, published as an arXiv preprint and under peer review, presents a quantitative framework for testing whether engineered particles could cross interstellar space, survive arrival on the Moon and remain identifiable in lunar dust. The researchers are not proposing a search for intact spacecraft. They would instead seek microscopic debris from spacecraft or other technological structures that could have reached the Moon after traveling between stars. Computer models assess whether refractory grains could survive interstellar travel and be carried toward the Moon by large-scale gas flows.
science.image_alt: Researchers propose searching Moon dust for alien technology

science.summary: New World screwworm, a parasitic fly, has returned to the United States while moving northward. The parasite has reached Texas and New Mexico, threatening livestock, wildlife, pets and, in rare cases, people. Researchers at the University of California San Diego have developed a tracking system to help predict where th
science.content: New World screwworm, a parasitic fly, has returned to the United States while moving northward. The parasite has reached Texas and New Mexico, threatening livestock, wildlife, pets and, in rare cases, people. Researchers at the University of California San Diego have developed a tracking system to help predict where the parasite could emerge next.

science.summary: Observations from the James Webb Space Telescope suggest that Chariklo's two rings appear different from previous views. Chariklo is a centaur, a class of objects with characteristics of both asteroids and comets. It is about 250 kilometers (400 miles) across and orbits between Saturn and Uranus.
science.content: Observations from the James Webb Space Telescope suggest that Chariklo's two rings appear different from previous views. Chariklo is a centaur, a class of objects with characteristics of both asteroids and comets. It is about 250 kilometers (400 miles) across and orbits between Saturn and Uranus.

science.title: Roman road study finds Antioch and Byzantium were better connected
science.summary: A multidisciplinary analysis of nearly 300,000 kilometers of Roman roads challenges the idea that the empire’s network centered on Rome. The analysis found that Antioch, Ancyra (modern Ankara), Byzantium and Corinth held more central positions for overland travel, while Rome remained important for Mediterranean maritim
science.content: A multidisciplinary analysis of nearly 300,000 kilometers of Roman roads challenges the idea that the empire’s network centered on Rome. The analysis found that Antioch, Ancyra (modern Ankara), Byzantium and Corinth held more central positions for overland travel, while Rome remained important for Mediterranean maritime navigation. Researchers used the Itiner-e digital atlas to analyze routes across an empire that covered about 5.5 million square kilometers at its height. The study found that Roman builders generally favored straight, gently graded roads where terrain allowed, but the network also included extensive secondary routes and often linked provincial capitals more directly to one another than to Rome.
science.image_alt: Roman road study finds Antioch and Byzantium were better connected

science.title: Study finds lunar water would limit million-person cities to a century
science.summary: A study by Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics researchers Martin Elvis and Jonathan McDowell estimates that a lunar city of 1 million people would exhaust available water in just over a century, even under highly favorable assumptions. Published in *Frontiers in Space Technologies*, the analysis assumes lunar
science.content: A study by Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics researchers Martin Elvis and Jonathan McDowell estimates that a lunar city of 1 million people would exhaust available water in just over a century, even under highly favorable assumptions. Published in *Frontiers in Space Technologies*, the analysis assumes lunar ice reserves of up to 1 billion metric tons and water-recycling efficiency of 98%. The researchers examined water and energy requirements for lunar populations of up to 1 million people. Under their assumptions, water availability, rather than energy generation, would limit settlement duration. The finding conflicts with proposals for rapidly expanding lunar cities, including Elon Musk’s stated vision of a self-growing city within 10 years.
science.image_alt: Study finds lunar water would limit million-person cities to a century

sports.title: Seahawks top NFL rankings as Week 2 approaches
sports.summary: The Seattle Seahawks enter Week 2 as the NFL.com power rankings' top-ranked team after Week 1, while the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Rams slipped behind them. ESPN’s poll also showed substantial movement after an unpredictable opening week. The San Francisco 49ers, Chicago Bears and New York Giants posted decisive W
sports.content: The Seattle Seahawks enter Week 2 as the NFL.com power rankings' top-ranked team after Week 1, while the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Rams slipped behind them. ESPN’s poll also showed substantial movement after an unpredictable opening week. The San Francisco 49ers, Chicago Bears and New York Giants posted decisive Week 1 results, while the Rams fell after a 27-7 loss to San Francisco in Melbourne and the Chargers dropped after losing at home to Arizona. Kansas City moved into the top 10 in the NFL.com ranking, and Week 2 begins Thursday with the 1-0 Buffalo Bills hosting the 1-0 Detroit Lions in the first regular-season game at Buffalo’s new Highmark Stadium.
sports.image_alt: Seahawks top NFL rankings as Week 2 approaches

sports.title: India seal Afghanistan T20 series after Samson’s 57
sports.summary: India defeated Afghanistan by seven wickets in the second T20I at New Delhi’s Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 15 to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Afghanistan made 159 for eight after India chose to field, with Nitish Kumar Reddy taking three wickets for 24 runs. India reached the target wit
sports.content: India defeated Afghanistan by seven wickets in the second T20I at New Delhi’s Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 15 to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Afghanistan made 159 for eight after India chose to field, with Nitish Kumar Reddy taking three wickets for 24 runs. India reached the target with 5.1 overs remaining. Sanju Samson led the chase with 57 from 22 balls, including seven fours and four sixes, while Abhishek Sharma added 39 from 19 balls. The opening pair put on 88 runs in 6.2 overs before both fell. Ishan Kishan then finished unbeaten on 38 alongside Tilak Varma, who made 15 not out.
sports.image_alt: India seal Afghanistan T20 series after Samson’s 57

sports.title: Real Madrid snatch late 3-2 win at Elche
sports.summary: Real Madrid defeated Elche 3-2 at the Martínez Valero on Tuesday, September 15, after Elche erased a two-goal lead before Real secured a fifth win in six La Liga matches. Arda Güler’s 25th-minute free kick deflected into the net off Elche goalkeeper Matías Dituro, and Kylian Mbappé doubled the advantage eight minutes l
sports.content: Real Madrid defeated Elche 3-2 at the Martínez Valero on Tuesday, September 15, after Elche erased a two-goal lead before Real secured a fifth win in six La Liga matches. Arda Güler’s 25th-minute free kick deflected into the net off Elche goalkeeper Matías Dituro, and Kylian Mbappé doubled the advantage eight minutes later after Yan Diomande’s cross. Elche responded after halftime through Abiel Osorio’s 71st-minute header and Fer Niño’s 83rd-minute equalizer. Substitute Carlos Espí scored in the first minute of added time from Mbappé’s pass, giving Real 15 points—level with Barcelona, which had played one fewer match at the time—and leaving Elche bottom with two points.
sports.image_alt: Real Madrid snatch late 3-2 win at Elche

sports.title: Former England forward Sterling pleads guilty to dangerous driving
sports.summary: Former England forward Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court on September 15 to dangerous driving, possessing six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen. The charges stemmed from a May 28 single-vehicle crash near the Minley interchange in Hampshire,
sports.content: Former England forward Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court on September 15 to dangerous driving, possessing six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen. The charges stemmed from a May 28 single-vehicle crash near the Minley interchange in Hampshire, after Sterling drove a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, M3, A327 and Minley Road. The court heard that witnesses reported erratic driving and saw a driver inhaling from a balloon before the Lamborghini struck roadside infrastructure. The crash caused substantial damage, including damage to all four wheels. Police said no other vehicle was involved and no one was injured. Sterling, 31, is without a club after making eight appearances for Feyenoord following spells at Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea and Arsenal.

sports.content: The World Athletics Council awarded Nairobi the 2029 World Athletics Championships at a meeting in Budapest on September 15, 2026. Kenya will become the first African country to stage the senior outdoor championships. Munich will host the 2031 edition, while Beijing is set to stage the 2027 event. London, Rome and Munich competed with Nairobi for the two hosting awards. Kenya’s bid cited its experience hosting international athletics competitions, planned upgrades to Kasarani Stadium and financial guarantees.

sports.content: Baltimore Orioles first baseman Pete Alonso hit his 300th career home run Tuesday, Sept. 15, at Citi Field against the New York Mets, his former team. His 414-foot solo shot off Kodai Senga tied the game at 3 in the ninth inning, and Alonso received a curtain call from 28,097 Mets fans despite playing for Baltimore. The Orioles won 7-5 in 11 innings when Coby Mayo hit a three-run inside-the-park home run. Alonso spent seven seasons with New York before joining Baltimore as a free agent last December. He left as the Mets' franchise home run leader with 264. The milestone came one night after his first return to Citi Field, when fans welcomed him with a tribute video, his former walk-up music and repeated ovations during a 2-1 Orioles win.

sports.content: Texas quarterback Arch Manning apologized Tuesday after laughing during Monday’s media availability about an AI-altered video that showed Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe. Asked about social-media edits following Texas’ 24-23 comeback victory over No. 1 Ohio State on Saturday, Manning called the fabricated clip “hilarious,” prompting criticism from sports journalists and social-media users. In an Instagram statement, Manning said his comment was insensitive, acknowledged that his words and actions had hurt people, and apologized specifically to Rowe for the consequences of his remarks. Rowe publicly accepted the apology and said she appreciated Manning taking accountability. The original postgame incident involved Sarkisian ending an on-field interview by shouting Texas slogans and walking away after Rowe tried to ask him a question.

sports.content: England beat Sri Lanka by 119 runs in the first T20 international at Southampton on September 15 to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series. Captain Harry Brook struck an unbeaten 114 from 49 balls, reaching his hundred in 42 deliveries, while Jos Buttler made 80 from 44 as England posted 254-4. The pair added 128 runs for the second wicket from 60 balls. Sri Lanka were bowled out for 135 in 19 overs after losing three wickets for 32 in the powerplay. England fast bowler Sonny Baker took 3-12 on his home ground, and debutant Aneurin Donald, brought in for the injured Phil Salt, made 12 from five balls. Brook’s innings was England’s joint-second-fastest T20I century, and the result extended England’s winning run against Sri Lanka in T20 internationals to 13 matches.
